newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips Q1 net from normal ops seen flat.
newsitem.headline: Philips Q1 net from normal ops seen flat.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV is set to announce little or no rise in first quarter net profit from normal operations, again handicapped by price pressures in cut-throat markets, analysts said.

Philips, which reports on Wednesday, is seen benefitting at the operating level from accountancy changes arising from its move to a passive minority holding in German loss-making affiliate Grundig. But net from normal ops is seen stagnating at around the 377 million guilders reported for first quarter 1996.
A Reuter poll put consensus at 366 million guilders with a range from 300 million to as high as 534 million.

"A number of main markets are still not very easy. A lot of the improvement should come from the book-keeping. I would be careful for the first two quarters of this year," said analyst Arjen Dibbets of MeesPierson.

"Most markets are flat or difficult. It's hard to think of a bright spot. The managerial side is improving, as are inventory levels. But a lot of the major markets are difficult or not improving significantly," he added.
Maarten Verbeek of Amstgeld said he was looking for income from operations for the quarter to rise to around 750 million guilders compared to the previous 690 million guilders.

"Some results will be clearly better, for example consumer products due to the divestment of Grundig. But, on the other hand, results from participations will drop because that will include Grundig. That's the counterbalance," said Verbeek.
Analysts are pencilling in first quarter operating profits of 100-150 million guilders from consumer products, up from a previous 52 million loss, as Grundig is stripped out.

But equity in income of unconsolidated companies is set to shrink from the 84 million first quarter 1996 gain as Philips uses that line to account for its 32 percent share of Grundig's performance, widely expected to be loss-making again.

The German consumer electronics company, whose results were absorbed by Philips at the operating level until the beginning of 1997, made a 1996 net loss of 553 million marks, but has predicted sharply lower operating losses for 1997.
Components and semi-conductors are expected to flag, with operating profit seen down to around 350 million guilders in the first quarter of 1997, against 496 million a year earlier.

"We've seen the figures of SGS Thomson where the (Q1) result halved. But you have to bear in mind that last year's figure was extremely good for SGS Thomson," said Verbeek, adding the Philips unit's performance was hard to judge accurately.

Analysts said they would be looking for further statements from the company on progress in its restructuring. Chairman Cor Boonstra has vowed to rid Philips of non-core and loss-making units, while straightening out management communication lines.
"I don't think that they will be really bullish before the end of the year," said Steven Vrolijk of ING Barings.

"The restructuring of companies which are still part of the firm will take another quarter or another two quarters to come through. What we now see is the positive effect of Grundig and all those names which they've sold, closed or are accounting for differently," he added. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
